_comment: ECS Task Definition - DevOps CI/CD Platform
_description: Complete task definition with all fields explained
_comment_family: family = task definition name. New versions increment: devops-cicd-platform:1, :2, :3
_comment_network: awsvpc = each task gets its own ENI (Elastic Network Interface). Required for Fargate. Gives task its own private IP in VPC subnet. Other modes: bridge (EC2 only), host (EC2 only)
_comment_launch: FARGATE = serverless, AWS manages servers. EC2 = you manage EC2 instances in cluster
_comment_memory: 512MB RAM for the entire task. Must match valid CPU/memory combination
_comment_execution_role: EXECUTION ROLE: used by ECS AGENT to: pull image from ECR, write logs to CloudWatch, read Secrets Manager. NOT your app's permissions. AWS provides: AmazonECSTaskExecutionRolePolicy
_comment_task_role: TASK ROLE: permissions your APPLICATION needs. S3 access, DynamoDB, SQS, etc. This is what your code uses when calling AWS SDK. Different from execution role!

containerDefinitions.name: app
containerDefinitions._comment_name: Container name. Referenced in: logs, exec commands, service discovery
containerDefinitions._comment_image: ALWAYS use specific SHA tag in production. Never :latest in production! SHA = immutable = reproducible

portMappings._comment: containerPort: port your app listens on. hostPort NOT specified for Fargate (awsvpc mode handles it)

containerDefinitions._comment_essential: true = if this container stops, the entire TASK stops. false = other containers keep running if this one dies. Set true for your main app container
containerDefinitions._comment_env: NON-SENSITIVE config. These appear in logs and console. Never put passwords here. Use secrets: for sensitive values
containerDefinitions._comment_secrets: SENSITIVE config from Secrets Manager or SSM Parameter Store. Injected as env vars at container start. NEVER in environment[] above. Requires execution role to read secrets
containerDefinitions._comment_logs: awslogs = send stdout/stderr to CloudWatch Logs. Group: /ecs/APP-NAME. Stream: app/CONTAINER/TASK-ID. Create group: auto-create if not exists. View: aws logs tail /ecs/devops-cicd-platform --follow
containerDefinitions._comment_health: ECS uses this to mark task healthy/unhealthy. interval: check every 30s. timeout: fail if > 5s. retries: 3 fails = unhealthy. startPeriod: grace period for startup (don't check first 60s)
containerDefinitions._comment_readonly: Matches Day 33/52 Docker security! Container cannot write to filesystem. Forces: all writes to mounted volumes
containerDefinitions._comment_user: Run as UID 1001 (non-root). Matches our Dockerfile: useradd --uid 1001
containerDefinitions._comment_linux: Drop ALL Linux capabilities (Day 33 pattern). initProcessEnabled: use PID 1 init process (handles zombie processes)
containerDefinitions._comment_mounts: readonlyRootFilesystem=true but /tmp needs to be writable. Mount in-memory volume for /tmp

_comment_volumes: Empty volume for /tmp mount. No host binding needed (Fargate manages it). Data lost when task stops
